# UNIT 2: Purification and Prayer (Taharah & Salah)
## Student Handout (Age 10)
---
*“Purity is half of faith.”* — Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)

---

### Welcome, Young Scholar!
Welcome to your student guide for Unit 2. In this unit, we will learn about how to clean ourselves externally (our bodies and clothes) and internally (our hearts) so we can talk to Allah five times a day. We will explore the teachings of the **Maliki school** of Islamic law (*fiqh*) and the **Ash'ari school** of Islamic belief (*aqidah*). 

As you read, you will see special terms in bold. These are Arabic words that scholars use. Make sure you learn their meanings!

---

## Page 2: The Creed (Aqidah) Connection — Why Do We Worship?

Before we learn *how* to wash or *how* to pray, we must ask a very important question: **Why do we worship Allah?**

### 1. Allah is Al-Ghani (The Self-Sufficient)
In our creed, we learn that Allah is **Al-Ghani** (الْغَنِيّ). This means He is completely rich and has no needs. 
*   Does Allah need our prayers? **No.**
*   Does Allah become stronger if we pray, or weaker if we don't? **No.**
*   Allah is the Creator of everything. He does not need anything from His creation.

### 2. We are the Needy Ones (Al-Fuqara')
We, the human beings, are **Al-Fuqara'** (الْفُقَرَاء) – the needy ones. We pray because we need Allah's help, love, guidance, and peace. Without prayer, our hearts get dusty and tired. 

### 3. Prayer is Gratitude (Shukr)
Imagine someone gave you a beautiful house, amazing food, and a loving family. What is the first thing you say? *"Thank you!"* 
Worship is our way of saying *"Thank you"* – **Shukr** (شُكْر) – to Allah for the gift of life, our bodies, our families, and Islam.

> **Creed Focus Box: Ubudiyyah**
> **'Ubudiyyah** (عُبُودِيَّة) means showing our love and humbleness to Allah by being His willing, happy servants. Salah is the best way to show our *'Ubudiyyah*.

---

## Page 3: Who Was Imam Malik?
To understand our school of law (*fiqh*), we should meet the teacher who started it: **Imam Malik ibn Anas** (إِمَام مَالِك).

*   **Where did he live?** He lived in **Madinah** (الْمَدِينَة), the city of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
*   **When was he born?** He was born in the year 93 AH, which was about 80 years after the Prophet (pbuh) passed away.
*   **How did he learn?** Imam Malik studied with the children and grandchildren of the Companions (*Sahabah*). Because he lived in Madinah, he got to see how the whole city practiced Islam every day.
*   **His famous book:** He wrote a book called **Al-Muwatta** (الْمُوَطَّأ), which means "The Approved Path." It is one of the earliest collections of Hadith and fiqh rulings in Islam!

---

## Page 4: The Importance of Purity (Taharah)

In Islam, we cannot stand in prayer unless we are clean. This cleanliness is called **Taharah** (طَهَارَة).

### What are we cleaning?
We must clean two things:
1.  **Outer Cleanliness:** Washing away dirt or physical impurities from our skin, clothes, and the place we pray.
2.  **Inner Cleanliness:** Cleaning our hearts from bad thoughts, anger, pride, and jealousy. 

### Two Types of Cleanliness Problems:
To understand purity, we need to know the difference between two things:
*   **Najasah (نَجَاسَة) - Physical Filth:** This is actual dirty stuff you can see or smell, like urine, blood, or stool. If it gets on your shirt, you just wash it off with water.
*   **Hadath (حَدَث) - Ritual State:** This is not physical dirt. It is a spiritual state of being unready for prayer. For example, if you sleep or use the bathroom, you aren't physically dirty all over, but you have entered the state of *hadath*. To exit this state, you must do Wudu or Ghusl.

---

## Page 5: Water — Our Best Friend for Purity

Allah sent down rain from the sky so that we can purify ourselves. But in Islamic law, not all liquids are the same! The scholars of the Maliki school divide water into three types. 

### The Three Types of Water:

```
                  +--------------------------------+
                  |         TYPES OF WATER         |
                  +--------------------------------+
                                  |
         +------------------------+------------------------+
         |                        |                        |
         v                        v                        v
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
|    Category 1    |     |    Category 2    |     |    Category 3    |
|  Ma' al-Mutlaq / |     |    Ma' al-Tahir  |     |   Ma' al-Najis   |
|     Tahur        |     |  (Pure, but NOT  |     | (Impure water)   |
| (Purifying water)|     |    purifying)    |     |  Cannot be used  |
|  Valid for Wudu  |     |  Cannot do Wudu  |     |  for anything    |
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
```

### 1. Al-Ma' al-Mutlaq / Al-Tahur (الْمَاء الْمُطْلَق / الطَّهُور)
This is natural water that has not changed. It is exactly as Allah created it. 
*   **Examples:** Rainwater, sea water, river water, well water, melted snow.
*   **Ruling:** It is **pure** in itself, and it has the power to **purify** other things. You **can** use it for Wudu and Ghusl.

---

## Page 6: Pure vs. Impure Water (Maliki Rulings)

### 2. Al-Ma' al-Tahir (الْمَاء الطَّاهِر)
This is water that was clean, but then a **pure** substance mixed with it and changed its color, taste, or smell completely. 
*   **Examples:** Water mixed with tea leaves (tea), water mixed with milk, chicken broth, or water mixed with a lot of soap.
*   **Ruling:** It is **pure** (tahir) – you can drink it or touch it – but it is **not purifying** (tahur). You **cannot** use it for Wudu or Ghusl!
*   **Maliki Detail:** If only a tiny bit of soap falls into water and doesn't change its look or smell, it is still *Tahur*. But if it changes the name of the water (so people call it "soap-water" instead of "water"), it becomes *Tahir* and cannot be used for Wudu.

### 3. Al-Ma' al-Najis (الْمَاء النَّجِس)
This is water that has been mixed with an **impurity** (*najasah*), like sewage, urine, or blood, and has changed its color, taste, or smell.
*   **Ruling:** It is dirty. You **cannot** drink it, touch it, or use it for Wudu.
*   **Important Maliki Distinction:** What if a tiny drop of blood falls into a bucket of water, but the water doesn't change color, taste, or smell? 
    *   In the Maliki school, if the water's qualities **do not change**, the water is still **Tahur** (purifying) and valid for Wudu. (However, if you have another clean bucket of water, it is disliked (*makruh*) to use this one). Other schools, like the Shafi'i school, say that if the water is a small amount, it automatically becomes impure even if it doesn't change.

---

## Page 7: Step-by-Step Wudu (Ablution)

To pray, we must make Wudu. In the Maliki school, Wudu has **seven obligations** (*Fara'id*). If you miss even one of these, your Wudu is invalid, and you must do it again.

### The 7 Pillars (Fara'id) of Wudu:
1.  **Intention (*Niyyah* - نِيَّة):** You make the intention in your heart to perform Wudu for prayer at the very moment you start washing.
2.  **Washing the Face (*Ghasl al-Wajh* - غَسْل الْوَجْه):** Washing from the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, and from ear to ear.
3.  **Washing the Arms (*Ghasl al-Yadayn* - غَسْل الْيَدَيْن):** Washing both arms from the fingertips up to and including the elbows.
4.  **Wiping the Entire Head (*Mash al-Ra's* - مَسْح الرَّأْس):** Wiping your wet hands over your **entire** head from the front hairline to the neck. Wiping the *entire* head is obligatory in the Maliki school (other schools allow wiping just a few hairs).
5.  **Washing the Feet (*Ghasl al-Rijlayn* - غَسْل الرِّجْلَيْن):** Washing both feet up to and including the ankles.
6.  **Rubbing (*Dalk* - دَلْك):** Gently rubbing each limb with your hand while washing it with water. (This is unique to the Maliki school! Simply letting water flow over your arms without rubbing is not enough).
7.  **Continuity (*Muwalat* - مُوَالَاة):** Doing all the steps of Wudu right after another without stopping. If you stop for so long that your skin dries, you must start over.

---

## Page 8: The Sunnahs and Recommended Acts of Wudu

Beside the obligations, there are actions that our beloved Prophet (peace be upon him) taught us to do. These are called **Sunnahs** (سُنَن) and **Fada'il** (فَضَائِل - virtues). 

### High Sunnahs of Wudu:
*   Washing your hands to the wrists at the very beginning (before washing the face).
*   Rinsing your mouth with water (**Madmadah** - مَضْمَضَة).
*   Sniffing water into your nose (**Istinshaq** - اِسْتِنْشَاق) and blowing it out (**Istinthar** - اِسْتِنْثَار).
*   Returning the wipe of your head (sliding your hands from the back of your neck back to the front).
*   Wiping your ears, inside and out.
*   **The Order (Tarteeb - تَرْتِيب):** Keeping the steps in order (washing face first, then arms, then head, then feet). 
    *   *Fiqh Check:* In the Maliki school, keeping the actions in order (*tarteeb*) is a highly recommended **Sunnah**, not an obligation. If you make a mistake and wash your feet before your face by accident, your Wudu is still valid, but you missed a Sunnah. You should try your best to always follow the correct order.

### Recommended Acts (Fada'il):
*   Saying *Bismillah* (In the name of Allah) at the start.
*   Using the tooth-stick (*Siwak*) to clean your teeth before Wudu.
*   Washing the limbs two or three times (the first wash is obligatory; the second and third are extra blessings).

---

## Page 9: Ghusl — The Ritual Bath

Sometimes, washing our hands and faces is not enough. We need to wash our entire body from head to toe. This ritual bath is called **Ghusl** (غُسْل).

### When is Ghusl Required?
Ghusl is required when a person enters a state of major impurity (*hadath al-akbar*). This happens in a few situations:
1.  **Major Impurity (*Janabah*):** Intimacy or physical emissions in sleep (like wet dreams).
2.  **Menstruation (*Hayd*):** When a woman's monthly bleeding ends.
3.  **Post-Natal Bleeding (*Nifas*):** When bleeding after childbirth ends.
4.  **Death:** When a Muslim passes away, we wash their body (*Ghusl al-Mayyit*).

### How to do Ghusl (The Obligations):
According to the Maliki school, there are **five obligations** for Ghusl:
1.  **Intention (*Niyyah*):** Intending to lift the major impurity.
2.  **Continuity (*Muwalat*):** Washing the whole body in one go without long breaks.
3.  **Rubbing (*Dalk*):** Rubbing your whole body with your hands while washing.
4.  **Washing the entire body:** Making sure water covers every single spot.
5.  **Permeating the hair (*Khilal al-Sha'r*):** Rubbing water down to the roots of all your hair.

---

## Page 10: Tayammum — Purification Without Water

What happens if you are in the desert and there is no water? Or what if you are very sick and water will make you worse? Allah is the Most Merciful, so He gave us a special way to purify ourselves using the earth. This is called **Tayammum** (تَيَمُّم).

### The Earth Substance: Sa'id (صَعِيد)
In the Maliki school, you can do Tayammum using anything that is a natural part of the earth's surface. This is called **Sa'id**.
*   **Allowed:** Clean soil, sand, rocks, stones, and natural dust.
*   **Not Allowed:** Wood, carpets, plastic, or anything man-made.

### How to Perform Tayammum:
1.  **Intention (*Niyyah*):** Intend in your heart to make prayer allowed.
2.  **First Strike:** Pat the clean earth or stone with both hands.
3.  **Wipe the Face:** Wipe your entire face once with your palms.
4.  **Wipe the Hands:** Wipe your hands and forearms. 
    *   *Fiqh Detail:* In the Maliki school, wiping to the wrists is obligatory (*Fard*), and wiping all the way to the elbows is a recommended **Sunnah**.

```
   [1. Intention] ──> [2. Pat the Earth] ──> [3. Wipe Face] ──> [4. Wipe Hands/Arms]
```

---

## Page 11: Salah — The Pillar of Religion

Once we are pure, we are ready for **Salah** (صَلَاة) – prayer. 

### Why is Salah the "Pillar of Religion"?
The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: *"Salah is the pillar of the religion (*'imad al-din* - عِمَاد الدِّين). Whoever establishes it has established the religion, and whoever destroys it has destroyed the religion."*
*   **The Tent Analogy:** Imagine a large tent. The center pole holding up the tent is the *'imad*. If you take away the center pole, the whole tent collapses. Similarly, prayer holds up our Islam. If we stop praying, our connection to Allah falls apart.

### The Five Daily Prayer Windows:
*   **Subh (Fajr):** Two units (*Rak'ahs*) at dawn.
*   **Zuhr:** Four units in the early afternoon.
*   **'Asr:** Four units in the late afternoon.
*   **Maghrib:** Three units immediately after sunset.
*   **'Isha:** Four units at night.

---

## Page 12: Standing in Prayer — The Position of the Arms (Sadl)

When we stand (*Qiyam*) during the obligatory daily prayers, where do we place our arms? 

### The Maliki Practice: Sadl (سَدْل)
In the Maliki school, the standard and most famous practice is **Sadl**. 
*   **Sadl** means letting your arms rest naturally and comfortably at your sides. You do not clasp your hands together on your chest.
*   *Why?* Imam Malik lived in Madinah. He watched the teachers, the descendants of the Companions, and the scholars of Madinah pray. Almost all of them prayed with their arms at their sides. This continuous practice is called **'Amal Ahl al-Madinah** (the practice of the people of Madinah).

### What about other schools?
*   Other Sunni schools (Shafi'i, Hanafi, and Hanbali) prefer **Qabd** (قَبْض) – clasping the right hand over the left hand on the chest or near the waist. 
*   **Fiqh Literacy Rule:** Both *Sadl* and *Qabd* are correct and sunnah. We must respect our brothers and sisters who clasp their hands, just as they respect us when we pray with our arms at their sides.

---

## Page 13: Summary Checklist of Wudu and Prayer

Let's review the main points you need to practice and memorize.

### My Wudu Checklist (The 7 Fara'id):
*   [ ] **Niyyah:** Did I make the intention in my heart at the start?
*   [ ] **Face:** Did I wash my face from my hairline to my chin, and ear to ear?
*   [ ] **Arms:** Did I wash my arms including the elbows?
*   [ ] **Entire Head:** Did I wipe my whole head from front to back?
*   [ ] **Feet:** Did I wash my feet including my ankles?
*   [ ] **Dalk:** Did I rub each limb with my hand as I washed it?
*   [ ] **Muwalat:** Did I wash everything quickly without stopping?

### The 5 Prayers & Rak'ahs:
1.  **Subh (Fajr):** 2 Rak'ahs
2.  **Zuhr:** 4 Rak'ahs
3.  **'Asr:** 4 Rak'ahs
4.  **Maghrib:** 3 Rak'ahs
5.  **'Isha:** 4 Rak'ahs

---

### Critical Reflection Question
Think about the difference between physical cleanliness (washing off mud or soap) and ritual purity (making an intention and performing Wudu). Why do you think Allah asks us to perform Wudu even if we are already clean from a shower? What does this tell us about the connection between our physical body and our spiritual soul? Write your thoughts in a short paragraph below.

# Assessment Questions: Purification & Prayer
## For Student Handout (Age 10)
---

### Part A: Multiple Choice (10 Questions)
*Select the best answer for each question.*

1.  **What does the Ash'ari creed teach us about Allah's attribute Al-Ghani?**
    *   a) Allah needs our prayers to be strong.
    *   b) Allah is completely rich and has no need for our worship.
    *   c) Allah only needs our prayers on Fridays.
    *   d) Allah needs us to clean the earth for Him.

2.  **Which of these is an example of Al-Ma' al-Mutlaq (Purifying Water)?**
    *   a) Apple juice.
    *   b) Chicken soup.
    *   c) Rainwater.
    *   d) Water mixed with a lot of soap.

3.  **If a cup of rosewater is mixed with plain water until it looks and smells completely like rosewater, what category of water does it become?**
    *   a) Al-Ma' al-Mutlaq (Purifying)
    *   b) Al-Ma' al-Tahir (Pure but non-purifying)
    *   c) Al-Ma' al-Najis (Impure)
    *   d) Natural water

4.  **According to the Maliki school, what happens if a tiny drop of blood falls into a bucket of water but does NOT change its color, taste, or smell?**
    *   a) The water becomes impure instantly.
    *   b) The water remains purifying (Tahur), but using it is disliked (Makruh) if other water is available.
    *   c) You must throw the bucket away.
    *   d) You can drink it but cannot do Wudu with it.

5.  **How many obligations (Fara'id) are there in Wudu according to the Maliki school?**
    *   a) 4
    *   b) 6
    *   c) 7
    *   d) 10

6.  **Which of these actions is unique/obligatory in the Maliki school of Wudu?**
    *   a) Rinsing the mouth.
    *   b) Rubbing the limbs with the hand while washing (Dalk).
    *   c) Saying Bismillah.
    *   d) Sniffing water.

7.  **What is the Maliki ruling on wiping the head during Wudu?**
    *   a) Wiping a few hairs is enough.
    *   b) Wiping the entire head is an absolute obligation (Fard).
    *   c) Wiping half of the head is enough.
    *   d) You only need to wipe your ears.

8.  **In the Maliki school, keeping the steps of Wudu in order (Tarteeb) is classified as a:**
    *   a) Fard (Obligation)
    *   b) Sunnah (Recommended practice of the Prophet)
    *   c) Makruh (Disliked act)
    *   d) Haram (Forbidden act)

9.  **What natural substance is NOT allowed for Tayammum?**
    *   a) Sand
    *   b) Clean soil
    *   c) Solid rock
    *   d) A wooden table

10. **The standard Maliki posture for arms during standing (Qiyam) in the obligatory prayers is:**
    *   a) Clasping hands on the chest.
    *   b) Clasping hands below the navel.
    *   c) Let the arms rest naturally at the sides (Sadl).
    *   d) Raising hands to the ears.

---

### Part B: Scenario-Based Questions (5 Questions)
*Read the scenario and choose or write the correct response based on Maliki rulings.*

11. **Yusuf is doing Wudu. He pours water over his right arm, but does not rub it with his hand. According to the Maliki school, is his Wudu valid?**
    *   *Answer:* No. Yusuf missed the obligation of **Dalk** (rubbing the limb with the hand). Simply letting water flow over the skin is not enough in the Maliki school.

12. **Amina is performing Wudu. Just as she finishes washing her face, her phone rings. She answers it and talks for 15 minutes. Her face is completely dry. She then washes her arms. Is her Wudu valid?**
    *   *Answer:* No. Amina broke the obligation of **Muwalat** (continuity). Because she paused for so long that her previous limb dried, she must start her Wudu over from the beginning.

13. **Zayd is traveling and cannot find any water to make Wudu. He decides to perform Tayammum. He finds a clean, solid limestone rock. Can he use this rock for Tayammum?**
    *   *Answer:* Yes. In the Maliki school, natural stone is considered **Sa'id** (natural surface of the earth) and is perfectly valid for Tayammum.

14. **Maryam is making Wudu. By mistake, she wipes her head before washing her arms. She remembers her mistake while washing her feet. What should she do according to the Maliki school?**
    *   *Answer:* Her Wudu is still valid because **Tarteeb** (order) is a Sunnah, not a Fard, in the Maliki school. However, to follow the Sunnah, she should wash her arms, then wipe her head, and then wash her feet in the correct order.

15. **Bilal stands up to pray Zuhr. He lets his arms hang naturally at his sides. His friend tells him, "Your prayer is invalid because you didn't cross your arms." How should Bilal respond?**
    *   *Answer:* Bilal should explain that letting the arms rest at the sides is called **Sadl**. It is the standard Sunnah practice of the Maliki school, based on the practice of the people of Madinah (*'Amal Ahl al-Madinah*). Both crossing the arms (Qabd) and letting them rest (Sadl) are valid sunnahs.

---

### Part C: Short Answer & Matching (5 Questions)
*Answer the questions briefly or match the terms.*

16. **Match the Arabic term to its correct definition:**
    *   1. *'Imad al-Din* -> ______ (Answer: Pillar of the Religion)
    *   2. *Najasah* -> ______ (Answer: Physical filth)
    *   3. *Hadath* -> ______ (Answer: Ritual state of impurity)
    *   4. *Shukr* -> ______ (Answer: Gratitude)

17. **Why is the prayer compared to the center pole of a tent?**
    *   *Answer:* Because if you pull out the center pole (*'imad*), the whole tent collapses. Similarly, prayer holds up our faith, and without it, our connection to Allah collapses.

18. **Name the five obligatory prayers in order, starting from the morning.**
    *   *Answer:* Subh (Fajr), Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, 'Isha.

19. **What are the three things that make Ghusl obligatory?**
    *   *Answer:* Major impurity (Janabah), completion of menstruation (Hayd), and completion of post-natal bleeding (Nifas).

20. **Why did Imam Malik prefer Sadl over crossing the arms in prayer?**
    *   *Answer:* He observed that the scholars and the descendants of the Companions in the city of Madinah prayed with their arms at their sides (*'Amal Ahl al-Madinah*).

---

## Answer Key
1. **b** (Allah is Al-Ghani, rich and free of needs)
2. **c** (Rainwater is natural water/Mutlaq)
3. **b** (It has changed its name to rosewater, so it is Tahir)
4. **b** (Water remains purifying/Tahur unless its qualities change, but is Makruh if other water is available)
5. **c** (7 obligations)
6. **b** (Rubbing - Dalk)
7. **b** (Wiping the entire head is a Fard)
8. **b** (Tarteeb is a Sunnah in the Maliki school)
9. **d** (Wooden table is not part of the natural earth surface)
10. **c** (Sadl - arms at the sides)
11. No, because rubbing (*Dalk*) is an obligation.
12. No, because she broke the obligation of continuity (*Muwalat*).
13. Yes, limestone is natural earth (*Sa'id*).
14. Her Wudu is valid because order (*Tarteeb*) is a Sunnah, but she should correct it to earn the Sunnah reward.
15. Explain that both Sadl and Qabd are authentic practices; Sadl is the standard Maliki way.
16. 1: Pillar of the Religion, 2: Physical filth, 3: Ritual state of impurity, 4: Gratitude.
17. It holds the religion together; without it, faith collapses.
18. Subh (Fajr), Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, 'Isha.
19. Janabah, Hayd, and Nifas (as well as death).
20. Because of the practice of the people of Madinah (*'Amal Ahl al-Madinah*).

# UNIT 2: The Jurisprudence of Purification and Prayer
## Student Handout (Age 13)
---
*“Cleanliness calls to faith, and faith is with its possessor in Paradise.”* — Imam Al-Tabarani

---

### Introduction: Developing Fiqh Literacy
As a young Muslim maturing in faith, it is time to move beyond simply memorizing actions and begin understanding the *legal framework* of Islam. This is called **Fiqh** (فِقْه) – the deep understanding of Islamic law. 

In this unit, we will study the rulings of **Taharah** (Purification) and **Salah** (Prayer) according to the **Maliki school** of jurisprudence, founded by Imam Malik ibn Anas (d. 179 AH) in the illuminated city of Madinah. We will also anchor our understanding in the **Ash'ari school** of theology (*aqidah*), which provides the logical framework of our beliefs. 

By understanding the logic behind different rulings, you will develop **fiqh literacy**—learning to appreciate the diversity of opinions (*ikhtilaf*) among scholars as a mercy, rather than assuming there is only one "universal" way to practice every detail.

---

## Page 2: The Theological Foundation — Worship and Divine Independence

To appreciate the rules of prayer, we must first understand *why* we pray from the perspective of Islamic creed (*aqidah*). 

### 1. The Independence of the Creator (Istighna')
In the Ash'ari school of creed, we study the necessary attributes of Allah. One of these attributes is **Qiyamuhu bi-Nafsihi** (قِيَامُهُ بِنَفْسِهِ) – Self-Existence or Self-Sufficiency. Allah is **Al-Ghani** (الْغَنِيّ), the absolutely Independent. 
*   **Allah does not benefit from our worship:** If every human and jinn on earth prayed with perfect devotion, it would not increase Allah’s majesty by a single atom.
*   **Allah does not suffer from our disobedience:** If the entire world refused to pray, it would not decrease His sovereignty.
*   **Why does He command us?** In His infinite wisdom and mercy, He commanded us to worship Him solely for *our* benefit. Worship is the path to our spiritual survival.

### 2. The Neediness of Creation (Iftiqar)
We are the creation, defined by **Iftiqar** (اِفْتِقَار) – utter dependency. We rely on Allah for our existence, our next breath, and our guidance. 
*   **Salah is a Rope:** Salah is the daily lifeline that connects the dependent servant (*'abd*) to the Independent Creator (*Al-Bari*).
*   **Salah as Gratitude (Shukr):** Cultivating *Shukr* is an intellectual and spiritual duty. Since Allah has given us life and everything we possess, regular prayer is the most direct physical expression of gratitude.

> **Key Term: 'Ubudiyyah**
> **'Ubudiyyah** (عُبُودِيَّة) is the state of slavery or servantship to Allah. It is not a state of forced oppression, but a state of loving submission where the human soul finds true freedom by serving the Creator rather than serving creation.

---

## Page 3: The Ash'ari Concept of Causality (Asbab)

A fundamental principle in the Ash'ari creed is our understanding of **causes and effects (*Asbab wa Musabbabat*)**. 

*   **No Inherent Power:** We believe that physical objects and actions have no independent power to cause effects. For example, fire does not burn by its own power; rather, Allah creates the burning *at the moment* the fire touches wood.
*   **Water and Purification:** Similarly, water does not possess an inherent, magical physical power to wash away a spiritual state like *hadath* (ritual impurity). 
*   **The Power of Command:** The purification occurs purely because we submit to **Allah’s command** to wash. When we do Wudu, we are using the physical means (*sabab*) out of obedience, but we believe that the true Creator of our spiritual purity is Allah.
*   **Tayammum Proof:** This is why, when water is missing, Allah commands us to wipe our faces with dry earth (*sa'id*). Physically, dirt doesn't clean us; but spiritually, it purifies us because we are obeying the Creator. The ritual itself is a training ground for submission.

---

## Page 4: The Historical Context of the Maliki School

To build your fiqh literacy, it helps to know how the Maliki school developed.

### 1. The Imam of Madinah: Malik ibn Anas
Imam Malik (93–179 AH) lived his entire life in Madinah, the city where the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) established the first Islamic society and where he is buried. Imam Malik was a student of the *Tabi'un* (the generation after the Companions), who in turn learned directly from the Companions (*Sahabah*).

### 2. The Practice of the People of Madinah ('Amal Ahl al-Madinah)
Imam Malik did not rely solely on written texts or single, isolated narrations (*Hadith Ahad*). He argued that the continuous, daily, public practice of the thousands of people living in Madinah was a stronger proof of the Prophet's practice. 
*   *Why?* The Prophet (pbuh) prayed in public in Madinah five times a day for ten years, in front of thousands of Companions. They taught their children, who taught their children. 
*   Imam Malik argued: *"The narration of thousands from thousands is more reliable than the narration of one person from one person."* This is a cornerstone of Maliki legal thought.

---

## Page 5: The Concept of Purification (Taharah)

In Islamic law, **Taharah** is a prerequisite (*shart*) for the validity of prayer. You cannot stand before Allah in a state of impurity.

### Outer vs. Inner Taharah
*   **Taharah al-Batin (Inner Purity):** This is the purification of the heart (*qalb*) from spiritual diseases such as pride (*kibr*), envy (*hasad*), showing off (*riya'*), and doubt. This is achieved through repentance (*tawbah*) and remembering Allah (*dhikr*).
*   **Taharah al-Zahir (Outer Purity):** This is the physical removal of impurities from the body, clothes, and place of prayer.

### The Two Barriers to Salah
To prepare for prayer, a student of fiqh must understand the two types of barriers:
1.  **Najasah (Physical Impurity):** A physical substance that is legally ruled dirty (e.g., urine, blood, pus, wine, stool, or dog saliva). If *najasah* lands on your body or clothing, it must be physically washed away with water.
2.  **Hadath (Ritual Impurity):** A non-physical, spiritual barrier. You cannot see *hadath*. It is a state that a person enters when they perform certain actions.
    *   **Hadath Asghar (Minor Impurity):** Triggered by sleeping, losing consciousness, or passing wind/using the bathroom. It is removed by performing **Wudu**.
    *   **Hadath Akbar (Major Impurity):** Triggered by intimacy, emissions, or the end of menstruation/post-natal bleeding. It is removed by performing **Ghusl**.

---

## Page 6: Water — The Instrument of Purification

Water is the primary means of removing both *najasah* and *hadath*. However, not all liquids are legally valid for ritual purification. In the Maliki school, water is systematically classified into three distinct categories based on its attributes: **color**, **taste**, and **smell**.

### 1. Al-Ma' al-Mutlaq / Al-Tahur (الْمَاء الْمُطْلَق / الطَّهُور)
*   **Definition:** Water that remains in its original, natural state, retaining all its natural characteristics (color, taste, and smell).
*   **Examples:** Rainwater, river water, sea water, spring water, well water, and melted snow.
*   **Ruling:** It is pure in itself (*tahir fi nafsihi*) and purifying for others (*mutahhir li-ghayrihi*). This is the **only** type of water that can remove *hadath* or wash away *najasah*.
*   *Note:* Natural changes (such as water standing for a long time, or containing natural elements like mud, algae, or sulfur from the ground) do not strip the water of its *Mutlaq* status.

---

## Page 7: Mixed Water and the Maliki Distinction

### 2. Al-Ma' al-Tahir (الْمَاء الطَّاهِر)
*   **Definition:** Purifying water that has been mixed with a **pure** (*tahir*) substance (e.g., soap, vinegar, milk, tea, perfume), causing a significant change in its color, taste, or smell.
*   **The Litmus Test:** Does it change the *name* of the liquid? If a bystander looks at it and says, *"That is tea"* or *"That is rosewater"* instead of simply *"That is water"*, it has lost its *Mutlaq* (unrestricted) status.
*   **Ruling:** It is pure (you can drink it, cook with it, and it will not make your clothes dirty), but it is **non-purifying**. You **cannot** use it to perform Wudu or Ghusl.

### 3. Al-Ma' al-Najis (الْمَاء النَّجِس)
*   **Definition:** Water that has been altered in color, taste, or smell by an **impurity** (*najasah*).
*   **Ruling:** It is impure. It cannot be used for Wudu, Ghusl, or drinking.
*   **The Crucial Maliki Distinction (No Qullatayn Threshold):**
    *   *What if a small impurity falls into water, but does NOT change its color, taste, or smell?*
    *   **The Maliki Position:** The water remains **Tahur** (purifying). Imam Malik argued that water is purifying by nature and cannot be made impure unless the impurity actually alters its characteristics. However, if the water volume is small, it is deemed **Makruh** (disliked) to use it for Wudu if alternative water is available.
    *   **Contrast with Other Schools:** The Shafi'i school rules that if water is less than **Qullatayn** (approx. 200 liters), it automatically becomes *najis* when an impurity falls into it, even if the color, taste, and smell remain completely unchanged. Understanding this difference helps you see how scholars looked at the same texts but deduced different, logical rules!

---

## Page 8: Step-by-Step Wudu — The Obligations (Fara'id)

In the Maliki school, a valid Wudu depends on **seven obligatory pillars (*Fara'id*)**. If you omit one of these, your Wudu is invalid.

### The 7 Fara'id of Wudu:

1.  **Intention (Niyyah - نِيَّة):**
    *   The resolution in the heart to remove ritual impurity or make prayer permissible.
    *   *Rule:* It must coincide exactly with the start of the Wudu (i.e., when you wash the face, or when you wash the hands at the start if you intend that wash as part of the Wudu).
2.  **Washing the Face (Ghasl al-Wajh - غَسْل الْوَجْه):**
    *   From the normal hairline to the chin, and from earlobe to earlobe. This includes washing through a thin beard.
3.  **Washing the Arms (Ghasl al-Yadayn - غَسْل الْيَدَيْن):**
    *   Washing both arms from the fingertips up to and including the elbows.
4.  **Wiping the Entire Head (Mash al-Ra's - مَسْح الرَّأْس):**
    *   Wiping the **entirety** of the head, from the front hairline to the nape of the neck.
    *   *Why?* Malikis hold that the Quranic command *"Wipe your heads"* requires covering the entire area. The Shafi'i school, however, allows wiping just a few hairs, while the Hanafi school requires wiping a quarter of the head.
5.  **Washing the Feet (Ghasl al-Rijlayn - غَسْل الرِّجْلَيْن):**
    *   Washing both feet up to and including the ankles.
6.  **Rubbing (Dalk - دَلْك):**
    *   Passing the hand over the body part during or immediately after pouring water, before the water dries. Malikis hold that water running over a limb is not "washing" (*ghasl*) without physical contact.
7.  **Continuity (Muwalat - مُوَالَاة):**
    *   Performing the steps consecutively without a delay that would allow the previously washed limb to dry under normal weather conditions.

---

## Page 9: The Sunnahs and Recommended Acts of Wudu

To achieve the full reward of the Prophet's (pbuh) method, we incorporate the **Sunnahs** and **Fada'il** (recommendations).

### The Sunnahs of Wudu:
1.  Washing the hands to the wrists at the beginning of Wudu (before washing the face).
2.  Rinsing the mouth (**Madmadah** - مَضْمَضَة).
3.  Sniffing water into the nose (**Istinshaq** - اِسْتِنْشَاق) and expelling it (**Istinthar** - اِسْتِنْثَار).
4.  Returning the wipe of the head (from the nape of the neck back to the front hairline).
5.  Wiping the ears (both the inner canals and outer surfaces).
6.  Using fresh water to wipe the ears (not using the water left over from wiping the head).
7.  **The Order (Tarteeb - تَرْتِيب):**
    *   *Fiqh Detail:* In the Maliki school, keeping the obligations in order (washing face, then arms, then head, then feet) is a **Sunnah**, not a Fard. If a person accidentally washes their feet before wiping their head, their Wudu is technically valid, though they have missed a Sunnah. In contrast, the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools classify *Tarteeb* as an absolute obligation (*Fard*).

### The Recommended Acts (Fada'il):
*   Saying *Bismillah* at the start.
*   Using the tooth-stick (*Siwak*).
*   Washing the limbs twice or three times (the first is Fard, the rest are Fada'il).
*   Minimizing the use of water to avoid waste (*israf*).

---

## Page 10: Comparative Analysis of Wudu (The Four Schools)

To help you build a broader fiqh literacy, let's examine how the four major Sunni schools view key steps of Wudu:

| Wudu Step | Maliki school | Shafi'i school | Hanafi school | Hanbali school |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Intention (*Niyyah*)** | Obligatory (*Fard*) | Obligatory (*Fard*) | Sunnah | Obligatory (*Fard*) |
| **Rubbing (*Dalk*)** | Obligatory (*Fard*) | Sunnah | Sunnah | Sunnah |
| **Wiping the Head** | Entire Head (*Fard*) | A few hairs (*Fard*) | Quarter of Head (*Fard*) | Entire Head (*Fard*) |
| **Order (*Tarteeb*)** | Sunnah | Obligatory (*Fard*) | Sunnah | Obligatory (*Fard*) |
| **Continuity (*Muwalat*)** | Obligatory (*Fard*) | Sunnah | Sunnah | Obligatory (*Fard*) |

---

## Page 11: Ghusl — The Ritual Bath

When a believer enters a state of major ritual impurity (**Hadath Akbar**), Wudu is insufficient. They must perform **Ghusl** (غُسْل) to restore their purity.

### When is Ghusl Required?
1.  **Janabah (Major Impurity):** Due to marital relations or emissions.
2.  **Hayd (Menstruation):** Once the menstrual flow ceases.
3.  **Nifas (Post-Natal Bleeding):** Once the post-childbirth bleeding ceases.
4.  **Death:** The ritual washing of a deceased Muslim.

### The Obligations (Fara'id) of Ghusl:
1.  **Intention (*Niyyah*):** Intending to lift the major impurity.
2.  **Continuity (*Muwalat*):** Performing the bath in one continuous session.
3.  **Rubbing (*Dalk*):** Rubbing the entire body with the hands.
4.  **Washing the Entire Body:** Ensuring water reaches every part of the skin, including the navel, underarms, and behind the knees.
5.  **Permeating the Hair (*Khilal al-Sha'r*):** Rubbing water to ensure it reaches the roots of all hair on the head, face, and body.
    *   *Note:* Unlike some other schools, the Maliki school does not require women to undo tight braids for Ghusl, *on the condition* that water can reach the scalp through the roots of the braided hair. If the braids prevent water from reaching the scalp, they must be undone.

---

## Page 12: Tayammum — Dry Purification

Islam is a practical religion designed to accommodate human weakness and changing circumstances. If water is unavailable or harmful to use, a believer performs **Tayammum** (تَيَمُّم).

### Conditions that Allow Tayammum:
*   **Absence of Water:** Having no water within a reasonable distance.
*   **Fear of Harm:** Using water would cause or worsen a severe medical condition, or the water is freezing and there is no way to heat it.
*   **Access Issues:** Water is present, but guarded by a dangerous animal or enemy, or the water is needed strictly for drinking to survive.

### The Legal Ground Substance: Sa'id (صَعِيد)
In the Maliki school, you must perform Tayammum on **Sa'id** (صَعِيد) – defined as the natural surface of the earth.
*   **Valid:** Soil, sand, solid stone, gravel, and natural dust.
*   **Invalid:** Any item that has been chemically altered, manufactured, or is organic but not part of the earth's crust (e.g., wood, carpets, textiles, plastic).

### The Steps of Tayammum (Maliki View):
1.  **Intention (*Niyyah*):** Intending to make prayer permissible (*istibahat al-salah*).
2.  **First Strike (*Al-Darbah al-Ula*):** Striking the *sa'id* with the palms of the hands.
3.  **Wiping the Face:** Wiping the entire face once.
4.  **Wiping the Hands and Arms:** Wiping the hands and forearms.
    *   *Fiqh Detail:* Wiping up to the **wrists** is the obligation (*Fard*). Striking the earth a second time and wiping up to the **elbows** is a recommended **Sunnah**.

---

## Page 13: Salah — The Spiritual Pillar and Cosmic Rhythms

Salah is not just a ritual; it is the center of a Muslim's day. It aligns our lives with cosmic cycles.

### The Concept of 'Imad al-Din (Pillar of Religion)
The Prophet (pbuh) taught us that Salah is the **'Imad al-Din** (عِمَاد الدِّين) – the pillar of the religion. In a physical structure, if the pillar is removed, the roof collapses. 
*   **In theology (Aqidah):** The Ash'ari creed teaches that Allah is independent of our prayers. However, our souls are created with a natural thirst to connect with the divine. Salah serves as the structural pillar of our spiritual life, protecting us from falling into heedlessness (*ghaflah*).

### The Cosmic Windows of Salah
The times of the five prayers are determined by the sun's position, linking our worship to the universe:
1.  **Subh (Fajr):** True dawn (*al-fajr al-sadiq*) until sunrise.
2.  **Zuhr:** From the sun's declination (*zawal*) from its meridian until the shadow of an object equals its height.
3.  **'Asr:** From the end of Zuhr shadow until the sun sets.
4.  **Maghrib:** From sunset until the red twilight (*al-shafaq al-ahmar*) disappears.
5.  **'Isha:** From the disappearance of the red twilight until true dawn.

### Preferred (Ikhtiyari) vs. Necessary (Daruri) Times
A unique feature of Maliki fiqh is the distinction between:
*   **Waqt Ikhtiyari (Preferred Time):** The window of time where a person is free to pray under normal conditions.
*   **Waqt Daruri (Necessary Time):** An emergency window (e.g., for someone who was asleep, ill, or traveling) that extends until the next prayer. Praying in this window is valid, but delaying it to this time without a valid excuse is sinful.

---

## Page 14: The Posture of Standing — Sadl in the Maliki School

When you pray in a congregation, you may notice different physical postures during the standing phase (**Qiyam** - قِيَام). 

### The Posture of Sadl (سَدْل)
In the Maliki school, the primary, dominant position for the arms during the standing portion of the obligatory prayer (*Fard*) is **Sadl** – letting the arms hang naturally and relaxed at the sides of the body.

### The Legal Evidences for Sadl:
1.  **'Amal Ahl al-Madinah (Practice of the People of Madinah):** 
    Imam Malik prioritized the inherited, continuous practice of the people of Madinah over isolated texts. He observed that the generation of the scholars, the children of the Companions, and the righteous of Madinah stood in prayer with their arms at their sides.
2.  **The Mudawwanah:**

        *   Discuss how this shifts our mindset: we do not pray to "do Allah a favor" or as a burden. Rather, we pray because we are *Al-Fuqara'* (the needy ones) who require spiritual connection, guidance, and peace. It fosters humility and sincere gratitude (*Shukr*).

16. **Why is the act of "Dalk" (rubbing) considered a logical requirement of washing in the Maliki school? Contrast this with the view of other schools.**
    *   *Suggested Outline:*
        *   Define *Dalk* (rubbing the skin during or immediately after pouring water).
        *   Explain the Maliki linguistic and legal analysis: Imam Malik argued that simply letting water flow over a surface is called "pouring" (*sabb*), not "washing" (*ghasl*). Since the Quran commands us to "wash" our faces and arms, we must perform *Dalk* for it to count as washing.
        *   Contrast this with schools like the Shafi'i or Hanafi, which hold that letting water cover the limb is sufficient to satisfy the command, even without physical rubbing.

17. **Discuss the textual and historical reasons why the Maliki school prefers the posture of "Sadl" (arms at the sides) during the standing phase of prayer.**
    *   *Suggested Outline:*
        *   Explain that Imam Malik lived in Madinah, the city where the Prophet (pbuh) lived and taught.
        *   Introduce the concept of *'Amal Ahl al-Madinah* (the practice of the people of Madinah) as a primary source of law. Imam Malik valued the continuous, generational practice of thousands of residents of Madinah over isolated written reports (*hadith ahad*).
        *   Reference the *Mudawwanah*, where Imam Malik stated that he disliked clasping the hands in obligatory prayers, preferring the natural hanging of the arms, which was the visible practice he inherited from the top scholars of the Prophet's city.

18. **Compare the rulings of the Maliki and Shafi'i schools on wiping the head (Mash al-Ra's) during Wudu. How does this differences showcase the concept of Fiqh Literacy?**
    *   *Suggested Outline:*
        *   Define the Maliki position: Wiping the *entire* head is an obligation (*Fard*).
        *   Define the Shafi'i position: Wiping even a few hairs is sufficient.
        *   Explain the linguistic root of the difference: the interpretation of the Arabic particle *Ba'* in the verse *"Wamsahu bi-ru'usikum"*. Shafi'is treat it as *tab'eed* (partitive - "some of"), while Malikis treat it as *za'idah* (extra emphasis - "wipe your heads").
        *   Discuss how this teaches us Fiqh Literacy: it shows that differences are not due to scholars making things up, but rather are the result of systematic, sincere, linguistic, and legal interpretations of the same Quranic text.

19. **Explain the wisdom behind the allowance of Tayammum. How does it connect to the Ash'ari creed concerning the relationship between means (asbab) and the Creator?**
    *   *Suggested Outline:*
        *   Explain the practical wisdom: mercy, easing hardship, and ensuring that the connection of prayer is never broken.
        *   Connect to Aqidah: Under Ash'ari creed, physical elements like water do not possess inherent, independent power to purify. Rather, Allah is the only Creator of effects. Water is simply a physical cause/means (*sabab*) that Allah usually uses. When He commands us to use earth (*sa'id*) instead, He demonstrates that the spiritual purity comes from obedience to His command, not from the physical properties of the elements.

20. **What is the distinction between Waqt Ikhtiyari (preferred time) and Waqt Daruri (necessary time) in Maliki Fiqh, and why is this distinction practically important?**
    *   *Suggested Outline:*
        *   Define *Waqt Ikhtiyari*: the normal time window for a prayer when one has free choice.
        *   Define *Waqt Daruri*: the emergency time window, extending beyond the preferred window, meant for people with legitimate excuses (illness, sleeping, menstruation ending).
        *   Discuss practical importance: It helps Muslims understand the severity of delaying prayers without an excuse, while offering reassurance and a clear legal path for those who face unavoidable emergencies.

# Presentation Slides: Purification & Prayer (Taharah & Salah)
## A Guide for Teachers (Maliki Fiqh & Ash'ari Aqidah)

---

# Slide 1: Welcome & Course Overview
## Purification & Prayer: The Journey of the Soul
*   **Subject:** Islamic Studies (Fiqh and Aqidah)
*   **Fiqh School:** Maliki (*Madhhab*)
*   **Creed School:** Ash'ari
*   **Core Focus:** Understanding how to purify ourselves externally and internally to stand before our Creator.
*   **Key Themes:**
    *   Water and Purity (*Taharah*)
    *   Ablution (*Wudu*) and Ritual Bathing (*Ghusl*)
    *   Dry Ablution (*Tayammum*)
    *   The Five Daily Prayers (*Salah*)
    *   The Posture of Standing in Prayer (*Sadl*)

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Welcome & Objective:** Welcome the students. Explain that this unit will cover how we prepare physically and spiritually to meet Allah in prayer.
*   **Pedagogical Note:** Highlight that we are learning the rulings according to the **Maliki school** of jurisprudence (*fiqh*) and the **Ash'ari school** of theology (*aqidah*). Explain that learning a specific school helps build "fiqh literacy"—understanding that while there is diversity in Islamic practice (*ikhtilaf*), each school is built on sound, systematic interpretations of the Quran and Sunnah.
*   **Discussion Starter:** Ask students: *"Why do you think we wash ourselves before talking to Allah? What does cleaning the body do for the heart?"*

---

# Slide 2: The Creed (Aqidah) Context: Why Do We Worship?
## Understanding 'Ubudiyyah (Servantship)
*   **Allah is Al-Ghani (The Independent):**
    *   Allah does not *need* our prayers or our worship.
    *   He is completely free of any need (*istighna'*).
*   **We are the Needy ones (*Al-Fuqara'*):**
    *   We pray because we are in need of Allah's mercy, guidance, and peace.
*   **Prayer as Gratitude (*Shukr*):**
    *   Worship is our natural response to the blessings of existence, sight, life, and faith.
*   **The Pillar of Religion (*'Imad al-Din*):**
    *   Prayer is the ultimate connection (*silah*) between the servant (*'abd*) and the Creator.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Ash'ari Creed Integration:** Explain the concept of *Al-Ghani* (The Rich/Self-Sufficient). Under Ash'ari theology, Allah's attributes include absolute independence. His commands (like prayer) are not for His benefit, but are out of His mercy to guide us. 
*   **Concept check:** Make sure students understand that when they pray, they are receiving the benefit, not Allah.
*   **Language Tip:** Introduce the terms *'Ubudiyyah* (the state of being a loving servant to Allah) and *Al-Ghani* (The One who has no needs).

---

# Slide 3: The Importance of Purity (Taharah)
## External and Internal Cleanliness
*   **What is Taharah?**
    *   Linguistically: Cleanliness and purification.
    *   Lawfully (*Shar'an*): Removing ritual impurity (*hadath*) and physical filth (*najasah*).
*   **The Two Levels of Purity:**
    1.  **Outer Purity (*Taharah al-Zahir*):** Clean clothes, clean body, and clean prayer area.
    2.  **Inner Purity (*Taharah al-Batin*):** Purifying the heart from pride, jealousy, and disbelief (*shirk*).
*   **Key Maliki Principle:** Purification is a strict requirement (*shart*) for the validity of prayer.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Explanation:** Distinguish between *hadath* (an invisible spiritual state of impurity, like after sleeping or using the bathroom) and *najasah* (a physical substance like urine or blood). 
*   **Pedagogical Tip:** Use the analogy of a computer screen: *Najasah* is like dust on the screen (you can see it and wipe it off), while *hadath* is like the screen being turned off (it's clean, but you need to press the power button—perform Wudu—to make it active).
*   **Reflection:** How does physical cleanliness help us focus mentally and spiritually?

---

# Slide 4: Types of Water — Overview
## The Legal Categories of Water
*   Water is the primary tool for physical purification.
*   In the Maliki school, water is classified into three main categories:
    1.  **Al-Ma' al-Mutlaq / Al-Tahur:** Purifying water.
    2.  **Al-Ma' al-Tahir:** Pure, but non-purifying water.
    3.  **Al-Ma' al-Najis:** Impure water.
*   **Rule of Thumb:** We must know which water is valid for Wudu and Ghusl.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Overview:** Introduce the idea that not all liquids that look like water can be used for ritual purification.
*   **Fiqh Literacy:** Clarify the distinction between "pure" (*tahir*) and "purifying" (*tahur*). A substance can be clean in itself (like orange juice) but you cannot use it to remove ritual impurity (*hadath*).
*   **Activity:** Show three transparent cups of liquid (1. Plain tap water, 2. Water mixed with milk/tea, 3. Water with a drop of vinegar or dirt). Ask students to predict which ones can be used for Wudu.

---

# Slide 5: Category 1: Al-Ma' al-Mutlaq (Purifying Water)
## Pure in Itself and Purifying for Others
*   **Definition:** Water that remains in its natural state, just as Allah created it.
*   **Examples:**
    *   Rainwater (*ma' al-matar*)
    *   Sea water (*ma' al-bahr*)
    *   Well water (*ma' al-bi'r*)
    *   River water (*ma' al-nahr*)
    *   Melted snow or hail
*   **Status:** It is **Tahur** (both pure to touch/drink and valid for Wudu and Ghusl).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Detailing the Ruling:** Even if well water contains some natural minerals or leaves that fell into it naturally, it is still classified as *Mutlaq* because these changes are natural and unavoidable.
*   **Hadith Reference:** Mention the Prophet's (pbuh) statement about the sea: *"Its water is purifying, and its dead meat is halal"* (Muwatta Malik).
*   **Key Question:** What makes well water or rain water different from apple juice, even though both are clean? (Answer: Well water is in its natural state and is called simply "water" without qualifiers).

---

# Slide 6: Category 2: Al-Ma' al-Tahir (Pure but Non-Purifying)
## When Pure Things Mix with Water
*   **Definition:** Purifying water (*mutlaq*) that has been mixed with a **pure** substance (e.g., milk, soap, rosewater, honey).
*   **The Key Maliki Ruling:**
    *   If the pure substance **changes** one of the three qualities of the water (color, taste, or smell) significantly so that it is no longer called just "water", it becomes **Tahir**.
*   **Examples:** Tea, coffee, rosewater, chicken soup.
*   **Status:** You **cannot** use it for Wudu or Ghusl, but it is clean to drink or cook with.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Maliki Specific Detail:** If a very small amount of soap or flour falls into water and doesn't change its name (people still look at it and call it "water", not "soap-water" or "dough-water"), it remains *Tahur* (purifying). The critical threshold is whether the *name* of the water has changed.
*   **Pedagogical Practice:** Emphasize this rule: "If it changes the name of the water, it changes its ruling."
*   **Discussion:** Why is it mercy that we cannot use juice or tea for Wudu? Imagine trying to pray with sticky juice on your arms!

---

# Slide 7: Category 3: Al-Ma' al-Najis (Impure Water)
## When Impurity Mixes with Water
*   **Definition:** Water that has been altered by an impurity (*najasah*), such as urine, blood, or sewage.
*   **The Maliki View on Water volume:**
    *   If the impurity changes the color, taste, or smell of the water, it is **Najis** (unanimously agreed).
    *   *What if an impurity falls into water but does NOT change its qualities?*
        *   **Maliki school:** The water remains **Tahur** (purifying) regardless of whether the volume is large or small. However, if the water is small in volume, it is disliked (*makruh*) to use if other water is available.
        *   *Contrast:* Other schools (like the Shafi'i school) rule that if the water is less than *Qullatayn* (approx. 200 liters), it automatically becomes *najis* even if it does not change.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy Focus:** Draw attention to this unique Maliki ruling. Imam Malik argued that water is purifying by default and only becomes impure if the impurity actually overpowers the water's qualities (taste, smell, color).
*   **Terminology:** *Qullatayn* refers to two large clay jars. Explain that while Shafi'is use this as a strict threshold, Malikis focus on the actual alteration (*taghyir*) of the water.
*   **Application:** If a drop of blood falls into a small bucket of water, and the water does not change color, smell, or taste, the Maliki ruling is that it is still valid for Wudu, though if you have another clean bucket, it is better (*makruh* to use the first).

---

# Slide 8: Step-by-Step Wudu (Obligations / Fara'id)
## The Core Pillars of Wudu
*   To have a valid Wudu, you must perform the **seven obligations (*Fara'id*)** according to the Maliki school:
    1.  **Intention (*Niyyah*)**
    2.  **Washing the Face**
    3.  **Washing the Arms** (including elbows)
    4.  **Wiping the ENTIRE Head (*Mash al-Ra's*)**
    5.  **Washing the Feet** (including ankles)
    6.  **Rubbing (*Dalk*)**
    7.  **Continuity (*Muwalat / Fawr*)**
*   Missing any of these seven invalidates the Wudu.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Introduction to Fara'id:** Explain that *Fara'id* (plural of *Fard*) are the absolute requirements of Wudu. If you miss one, even by mistake, your Wudu is not complete and your prayer is invalid.
*   **Memory Tool:** Encourage students to write down or memorize the number **7** for Maliki Wudu obligations. (Other schools have fewer; e.g., Shafi'is have 6, Hanafis have 4).
*   **Pronunciation:** Pronounce *Dalk* (dal-lam-kaf) and *Muwalat* (meem-waw-alif-lam-alif-ta) clearly.

---

# Slide 9: Focus on Wudu Fara'id: Niyyah, Face, and Arms
## Starting the Wudu Correctly
*   **1. Intention (*Niyyah*):**
    *   Must be made in the heart at the very moment you begin washing.
    *   Formulated as: intending to perform Wudu for prayer, or to remove ritual impurity.
*   **2. Washing the Face (*Ghasl al-Wajh*):**
    *   From the normal hairline to the bottom of the chin, and from earlobe to earlobe.
*   **3. Washing the Arms (*Ghasl al-Yadayn*):**
    *   From the fingertips up to and including the elbows.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Niyyah Details:** In the Maliki school, the intention must coincide with the start of the Wudu. If you wash your hands at the beginning as a habit without intending Wudu, and only make the intention when washing your face, the initial hand washing does not count as part of Wudu.
*   **Face Details:** Remind students that washing the beard is required. If the beard is thin, the skin underneath must be washed. If it is thick, washing the exterior is sufficient.
*   **Elbows:** Emphasize that the elbow is *included* in the wash, not excluded.

---

# Slide 10: Wiping the Entire Head (Mash al-Ra's)
## A Key Maliki Distinction
*   **4. Wiping the Head (*Mash*):**
    *   You must wipe your hands over the **entire head**—from the front hairline all the way to the nape of the neck.
*   **The Maliki View:**
    *   Wiping the *entire* head is an absolute obligation (*Fard*).
*   **Comparison with Other Schools:**
    *   **Shafi'i:** Wiping even a few hairs is sufficient.
    *   **Hanafi:** Wiping a quarter of the head is required.
    *   **Hanbali:** Wiping the entire head is also obligatory.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy:** Point out this major difference. Explain that the difference comes from how scholars interpreted the Arabic letter *Ba'* in the Quranic verse: *"Wamsahu bi-ru'usikum"* (Wipe [part of or all] your heads). 
    *   Imam Malik interpreted the *Ba'* as extra emphasis (*za'idah*), meaning "Wipe your heads [entirely]." 
    *   Imam al-Shafi'i interpreted it as *tab'eed* (partitive), meaning "Wipe a part of your heads."
*   **Demonstration:** Show how to place wet thumbs on the temples and index fingers on the front hairline, then slide the hands back to the neck. Note: The return motion (from back to front) is *Sunnah*, not *Fard*.

---

# Slide 11: Rubbing (Dalk) and Continuity (Muwalat)
## Distinctive Maliki Obligations
*   **6. Rubbing (*Dalk*):**
    *   Passing the hand over the body part while washing it, or immediately after pouring water, before it dries.
    *   *Why?* Merely letting water run over the skin is not considered "washing" (*ghasl*) in Maliki fiqh; it must be rubbed.
*   **7. Continuity (*Muwalat* / *Fawr*):**
    *   Performing the steps of Wudu one after another without any long interruption that would allow the previous limb to dry under normal weather conditions.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Rubbing (*Dalk*):** Explain that this is unique to the Maliki school. If someone just stands under a faucet and lets water pour over their arms without rubbing them, their Wudu is invalid according to Imam Malik.
*   **Continuity (*Muwalat*):** Explain that if someone starts Wudu, washes their face, and then stops to answer a phone call for 10 minutes until their face dries, they must start Wudu all over again.
*   **Exception:** If someone runs out of water and goes to get some immediately, they can continue where they left off, provided the delay was not unreasonably long.

---

# Slide 12: Sunnan and Fada'il of Wudu
## Enhancing Our Purification
*   **Sunnahs of Wudu (High Sunnahs):**
    *   Washing the hands to the wrists at the beginning.
    *   Rinsing the mouth (*Madmadah*).
    *   Sniffing water into the nose (*Istinshaq*) and blowing it out (*Istinthar*).
    *   Returning the wipe of the head (from the neck back to the front).
    *   Wiping the ears inside and out.
    *   Renewing the water for the ears.
    *   **The Order (*Tarteeb*):** Keeping the obligatory actions in their correct order. (In Maliki fiqh, *tarteeb* is a Sunnah, not a Fard, but skipping it deliberately is disliked).
*   **Recommended Acts (*Fada'il* / *Mustahabbat*):**
    *   Saying *Bismillah* at the start.
    *   Using the tooth-stick (*Siwak*).
    *   Washing three times (the first wash is Fard, second and third are Fada'il).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Clarifying Tarteeb:** Note that in the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools, *Tarteeb* is a Fard (obligation). In the Maliki school, it is a Sunnah. This means that if someone accidentally washes their feet before wiping their head, their Wudu is still technically valid, though they have missed a Sunnah. They should correct it if they remember during the Wudu.
*   **Class Activity:** Ask students: *"If Wudu order is a Sunnah, why should we still try to keep it in order?"* Explain that following the Sunnah brings immense reward and aligns us with the practice of the Prophet (pbuh).

---

# Slide 13: Ghusl — The Ritual Bath
## Restoring Major Ritual Purity
*   **What is Ghusl?**
    *   Washing the entire body with purifying water (*mutlaq*) with a specific intention.
*   **When is it Required?**
    1.  **Major Impurity (*Janabah*):** Due to marital intimacy or physical emissions.
    2.  **Completion of Menstruation (*Hayd*):** For women.
    3.  **Completion of Post-Natal Bleeding (*Nifas*):** For women.
    4.  **Death:** Washing the deceased believer (*Ghusl al-Mayyit*).
*   **Status:** An absolute obligation to perform prayer and enter the mosque.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Pedagogical Sensitivity:** Discuss these topics maturely. Frame Ghusl as a blessing that transitions a believer from a state of ritual restriction back to full connection in worship.
*   **Vocabulary:** Define *Hadath al-Akbar* (major ritual impurity, which requires Ghusl) versus *Hadath al-Asghar* (minor ritual impurity, which only requires Wudu).

---

# Slide 14: Steps and Obligations of Ghusl
## The Maliki Method of Ghusl
*   **The Obligations (*Fara'id*) of Ghusl (5 items):**
    1.  **Intention (*Niyyah*):** To lift the major impurity.
    2.  **Continuity (*Muwalat*):** Not pausing so long that part of the body dries.
    3.  **Rubbing (*Dalk*):** Rubbing the entire body with the hand.
    4.  **Washing the entire body:** Ensuring water reaches every part.
    5.  **Permeating the hair (*Khilal al-Sha'r*):** Rubbing water to the roots of all hair (head, beard, etc.).
*   **How to do it (Sunnah Method):**
    *   Wash hands, wash private parts, perform Wudu (except feet, or complete it), pour water over the head three times rubbing the scalp, wash the right side of the body, then the left side, ensuring no spot is missed.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Dalk in Ghusl:** Emphasize that rubbing is required. If a person just stands under a shower without rubbing their skin with their hands, their Ghusl is invalid according to the Maliki school.
*   **Difficult Areas:** Remind students to pay attention to hidden areas like the navel, underarms, backs of knees, and between the toes.
*   **Hair:** Explain that women do not need to undo tight braids for Ghusl in the Maliki school, *provided* the water can reach the roots of the hair. If the water cannot reach the roots, the braids must be undone.

---

# Slide 15: Tayammum — Purification with Earth
## Allah's Mercy When Water is Unavailable
*   **What is Tayammum?**
    *   Dry purification using clean, natural earth.
*   **When is it Allowed?**
    *   **Lack of Water:** No water is nearby, or the water available is only enough for drinking.
    *   **Inability to Use Water:** Due to severe illness, wound, or extreme cold that would cause harm, and there is no way to heat it.
*   **Spiritual Lesson:**
    *   Tayammum teaches us that purification is primarily a spiritual act of obedience. If the physical means (water) are missing, we still submit to the ritual using earth.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Spiritual Insight (Ash'ari):** Connect this to Aqidah. Allah is the Creator of both water and earth. He is the One Who purifies us; the water and earth are merely means (*asbab*). When the primary means (water) is removed, Allah makes the secondary means (earth) valid. This shows that the power to purify comes from Allah's command, not the physical properties of water.
*   **Quranic Verse:** Mention Surah al-Ma'idah (5:6): *"And if you are ill or on a journey... and find no water, then perform Tayammum with clean earth..."*

---

# Slide 16: The Steps and Substance of Tayammum
## What is "Sa'id" and How is it Wiped?
*   **The Ground Substance (*Sa'id*):**
    *   In the Maliki school, *Sa'id* is defined as anything that is part of the natural surface of the earth.
    *   This includes: Clean soil/dirt, sand, natural stone/rocks, pebbles, and dust.
*   **The Step-by-Step Method:**
    1.  **Intention (*Niyyah*):** Intending to make prayer permissible (*istibahat al-salah*).
    2.  **First Strike:** Gently pat the earth/stone with both palms.
    3.  **Wipe the Face:** Wipe the entire face once.
    4.  **Second Strike (Sunnah) / Wipe the Hands:** Wipe the hands and forearms. In the Maliki school, wiping to the wrists is Fard, and wiping up to the elbows is Sunnah.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Maliki Scope of Sa'id:** Point out that Malikis are very flexible about the substance. You can make Tayammum on a solid rock or clean sand, whereas some other schools require soil that has loose dust that clings to the hands.
*   **First Strike / Second Strike:** Clarify that hitting the ground once is Fard. Wiping up to the wrists is Fard. Hitting a second time and wiping up to the elbows is Sunnah in the Maliki school.
*   **Wiping Method:** Show how to wipe the right arm first (using the left hand) and then the left arm (using the right hand).

---

# Slide 17: The Five Daily Prayers (Salah)
## The Pillar of Religion (Imad al-Din)
*   **Why is Salah the Pillar?**
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) said: *"The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer, and its peak is Jihad"* (Tirmidhi).
*   **The Metaphor of the Pillar:**
    *   Just like a tent collapses if the main central pole (*'imad*) is pulled out, a person's practice of Islam cannot stand without Salah.
*   **The Five Obligatory Prayers (*Al-Salawat al-Khams*):**
    1.  **Subh / Fajr** (Dawn)
    2.  **Zuhr** (Midday)
    3.  **'Asr** (Afternoon)
    4.  **Maghrib** (Sunset)
    5.  **'Isha** (Night)

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Discussion:** Why do you think prayer is called a "pillar"? What happens to our day when we miss a prayer?
*   **Term Check:** Explain that in North Africa and West Africa (heavily Maliki regions), the dawn prayer is often called **Subh** for the two obligatory units, while the term **Fajr** is sometimes used specifically for the highly recommended two Sunnah units performed just before it. We will use them interchangeably for the obligatory dawn prayer here, but mention this regional terminology.

---

# Slide 18: Prayer Times & Cosmic Rhythms
## Aligning Our Day with Creation
*   Each prayer has a specific window of time linked to the movement of the sun:
    *   **Subh (Fajr):** Starts at true dawn (*al-fajr al-sadiq*) and ends at sunrise.
    *   **Zuhr:** Starts when the sun passes its highest point (zenith/*zawal*) and ends when the shadow of an object equals its height.
    *   **'Asr:** Starts when Zuhr ends and ends when the sun sets (preferred time ends when sun turns yellow).
    *   **Maghrib:** Starts immediately after sunset and ends when the red twilight (*al-shafaq al-ahmar*) disappears.
    *   **'Isha:** Starts when the red twilight disappears and ends at dawn (preferred time ends at the first third of the night).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Understanding Times:** In Maliki fiqh, there are two types of time for each prayer:
    1.  *Ikhtiyari* (Preferred time): The window in which you should pray under normal circumstances.
    2.  *Daruri* (Necessary/Emergency time): The window for those with valid excuses (like sleeping, illness, menstruation ending) to pray before the prayer is considered missed (*qada'*).
*   **Cosmic Connection:** Point out that Islam connects our worship directly to nature. We look at the sun and shadows, connecting our souls to the natural cycles created by Allah.

---

# Slide 19: How We Stand in Prayer — The Position of the Arms
## Standing (Qiyam) and Sadl
*   **Qiyam (Standing):**
    *   Qiyam is an obligatory pillar (*Rukn*) of the obligatory prayers.
*   **Where do we put our arms?**
    *   There are two main practices among Muslims during standing:
        1.  **Sadl:** Letting the arms rest naturally at the sides of the body.
        2.  **Qabd:** Clasping the right hand over the left hand/wrist on the chest or below the navel.
*   **The Maliki View:**
    *   In the dominant Maliki opinion, **Sadl** is the preferred and sunnah way to stand during obligatory prayers (*Fara'id*).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Clarification:** Many students may see Muslims clasping their hands and assume this is the only way to pray. Explain that **Sadl** is a very ancient, valid practice.
*   **Diversity in Fiqh:** Emphasize that all four Sunni schools are correct. Shafi'is, Hanafis, and Hanbalis perform *Qabd* (with slight variations on placement). Malikis perform *Sadl*. 
*   **Class Activity:** Ask students to try both postures. Ask: *"How does it feel to stand in Sadl? Does it feel relaxed and natural?"* Explain that both ways are inherited from the Prophet (pbuh).

---

# Slide 20: Understanding Sadl (Arms at the Sides)
## The Background of the Maliki Practice
*   *Why do Malikis perform Sadl?*
    1.  **The Practice of Madinah (*'Amal Ahl al-Madinah*):** Imam Malik lived in Madinah, the city of the Prophet (pbuh). He observed that the scholars and descendants of the Companions prayed with their arms at their sides.
    2.  **The Mudawwanah:** The primary textbook of Maliki fiqh quotes Imam Malik saying that he disliked clasping the hands in obligatory prayers, preferring that the arms rest naturally.
*   **Nafl (Voluntary) Prayers:**
    *   Imam Malik permitted clasping (*qabd*) in voluntary prayers if the prayer is long and the person needs to rest their arms.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Contextual Depth:** Explain the concept of *'Amal Ahl al-Madinah* (the practice of the people of Madinah). For Imam Malik, the continuous, inherited practice of thousands of people in Madinah who learned directly from their fathers (who learned from the Companions) was a stronger source of law than a single isolated narration (*hadith ahad*).
*   **Respecting Differences:** Reiterate that we do not look down on others who pray differently. A Maliki student standing in *sadl* next to a Shafi'i student in *qabd* are both praying correctly according to authentic traditions.

---

# Slide 21: Summary & References
## Taking it Forward
*   **What We Learned:**
    *   How to categorize water (Mutlaq, Tahir, Najis).
    *   The 7 Fara'id of Wudu, featuring *Mash* of the entire head, *Dalk*, and *Muwalat*.
    *   The essential obligations of Ghusl and Tayammum.
    *   The prayer times and standing in *Sadl*.
*   **Primary Sources of the Maliki School:**
    *   *Al-Muwatta* of Imam Malik
    *   *Al-Mudawwanah al-Kubra* of Sahnun / Ibn Qasim
    *   *Al-Risalah* of Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani
    *   *Al-Kafi* of Ibn Abd al-Barr

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Review Quiz:** Ask quick recall questions (e.g., *"How many obligations are there in Maliki Wudu?"*, *"Can you do Wudu with rosewater?"*, *"What is Sadl?"*).
*   **Homework/Reflection:** Distribute the student handouts. Ask students to read the sections on Wudu and practice the steps at home, paying special attention to *Dalk* (rubbing) and wiping the whole head.
*   **Final thought:** End with a reminder that physical cleanliness is the key that unlocks our connection with Allah in Salah.
